decisions.quote:
We find that the
main findings could be reproduced successfully and that they hold even when using a
modelling approach based on the frequentist framework. While we did find some issues
related to the code provided, the reporting of the coefficients, and some inconsistencies
between the preregistration and the article, they were minor and did not clash with the
overall narrative of the paper.
decisions.reason: Under the Axis 1 codebook rules, 'computationally reproducible' encompasses both rounding and negligible numerical differences (as well as script corrections such as fixing 'newdata' to 'data' and exponentiating log-odds to match reported odds ratios), whereas 'computational issues' requires unrecovered results or discrepancies treated as substantive. Across Section 2, Table 1, Table 2, and Section 6, the authors show that point estimates match after exponentiating and rounding/truncating, characterize the remaining credible interval differences as small and not affecting the authors' claims, mark the study as 'Fully' reproducible from both raw and analysis data in Table 1 ('fulfilled all the reproducibility criteria'), and conclude that the main findings were reproduced successfully with only minor issues.

scope_review.parent_objection: First reply treats any CI difference beyond rounding as computational issues. Exact axis1 codebook allows rounding AND negligible numerical differences, and issues when discrepancies are treated as substantive. Source computational section says ultimately all reproducibility criteria fulfilled; coefficients match after exponentiating; CI differences small and do not affect claims; Conclusion says main findings reproduced successfully and issues minor. Settle whether these differences qualify as negligible numerical differences under exact codebook or substantive failure to recover central numbers. Read full computational section, Conclusion, and Table2; do not silently equate beyond-rounding with substantive. Outcome_robustness is separate. Return requested axis with shortest sufficient contiguous quote.

prior_reply.quote: While in those instances the coefficients match after exponentiating, many of the credible intervals (CrI) still don’t match – we are not sure why that is. The differences are small and don’t affect the claims made by the authors, but they go beyond what could be explained by rounding error.
prior_reply.reason: Although the main substantive claims held, Axis 1 evaluates whether the original reported numbers were recovered; the authors explicitly report that many credible intervals (as well as some reported point estimates in Table 2) could not be recovered and differed beyond rounding error, which matches 'computational issues'.
